claim_scope.question: How many tokens can a DFlash-style speculator propose and usefully accept per target verification for Gemma 4 31B?
workloads: public reasoning, code, and chat benchmarks
the lab's synthetic c32 endpoint workload

decision: Use the released 2B Gemma 4 DFlash drafter as the next serious speculation baseline. Test 8, 12, and 16-token blocks on the current runtime and hardware, and select by matched whole-request cost rather than acceptance alone. Do not extrapolate the 46k-parameter CPU copy-decoder negative to DFlash.

local_measured.old_h200_dflash_runtime_decision: Depth 4 had the lowest summed draft-plus-verifier CUDA-event cost in the older SGLang H200 c32 sweep; the request consumer for the depth sweep was invalid, so this is not acceptance evidence.
local_measured.synthetic_c32_interpretation: The synthetic completions are highly repetitive. This is an offline workload ceiling and not a realistic traffic estimate.

z_lab_b300_acceptance_length.metric_definition: Acceptance length follows the standard total committed tokens per verification convention and includes the target bonus token. Approximate accepted draft tokens equal acceptance length minus one.
z_lab_b300_acceptance_length.note: Single B300, vLLM, greedy, thinking enabled, maximum 4096 output tokens; reported acceptance length is nearly invariant from c1 to c32.

modal_custom_training.claim: Application-specific fine-tuning has increased acceptance length from about 3 to over 9.
modal_custom_training.data_scale: tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of application tokens

estimate.application_tuned_possible_accepted_leng: 9+ on a narrow stable domain, vendor-reported
estimate.generic_code_math_reasoning_accepted_dra: 5-8, corresponding to acceptance length 6-9 including the bonus token
estimate.generic_mixed_chat_accepted_draft_tokens: 2-4, corresponding to acceptance length 3-5 including the bonus token
estimate.recommended_planning_blend_before_measur: 4-6 accepted draft tokens, or 5-7 total committed tokens including the target bonus, per verification on a mixed reasoning/code-heavy serving workload

falsification_rule: Reject the planning estimate if a request-disjoint workload-matched run on the target hardware produces less than 4 mean accepted tokens or if whole-request output-token cost fails to improve despite higher acceptance.
limitations: Acceptance length is workload-, generation-position-, model-, runtime-, hardware-, concurrency-, and sampling-dependent.
Acceptance length is not speedup: draft latency, target verification geometry, scheduler overhead, and batch saturation determine whole-request cost.
The Z Lab B300 model-card result is vendor-reported and not yet reproduced by this lab.
The older lab H200 depth sweep used an earlier SGLang integration and did not have a valid response consumer for acceptance measurement.
next_action: Run the released Gemma 4 DFlash checkpoint without training first on a realistic request-disjoint mix, using the newest supported vLLM PR or SGLang Spec V2. Measure acceptance by position, draft and verifier wall time, whole-request throughput, and price-normalized output-token cost at c1, c8, and c32. Fine-tune only after this stock baseline.
